deep.reconstruction:
This page is an observation log, not a derivation. Its title, 'Libellenjournal', means journal of the spirit level; 'Kreis in Osten' means circle in the East position. It continues the previous page, where on April 23 Gauss determined the scale value of the main level: readings were reduced with 1'' = 1.8 mm, with the 'Spitzen nach innen' (points inward) position. This suggests the level of the Göttingen meridian circle, though the instrument identification is my inference. The year is not stated; the following page is dated 1832, but the bundle is miscellaneous, so the date cannot be fixed from this page.

For each date (April 24 – May 18) four quantities are entered:
- Columns 1–3 are angular readings in arcminutes and arcseconds (e.g. 9'20.9'', 4'11.5'', 3'22.8''). They are probably microscope or level readings taken at different places or positions.
- Column 4, headed 'i−a', is a small positive quantity in arcseconds (+0.53'' to +7.40''). It is plausibly 'innen − außen' (inside minus outside) or an inclination-type difference. That reading is uncertain.

Interspersed notes record instrumental interventions:
- 'Mikroskope berichtiget' (microscopes adjusted) after April 24.
- 'Unteres Mikroskop geschoben' (lower microscope shifted) on April 28. After this, column 1 jumps from about 9'07'' to about 3'26''. This confirms that column 1 is the lower-microscope reading and that the shift was about 5'40''.
- 'Schnüre kürzer gebunden' (cords tied shorter) before April 30.

From April 30 onward, columns 1–3 drift slowly downward by about 1'' per few days. Column 4 fluctuates without trend, with a mean of about 3.6''.

No arithmetic relation among columns 1–3 and column 4 can be confirmed from the page. Column 4 is neither their mean nor a simple difference, so it is presumably derived from level-bubble end readings not copied here. There is no mathematical derivation to reconstruct.
errors: No computational steps are shown, so none can be checked. Column 4 cannot be reproduced from columns 1–3 and must depend on unrecorded level-end readings.

results.what: Daily log of instrument (level/microscope) readings on an astronomical circle, with notes on instrumental adjustments
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice of observatory astronomers (Bessel, Gauss, Struve, et al.)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observatory log of level and microscope readings with no mathematical content. Gauss's practical astronomical work at Göttingen with the meridian circles is well documented.

checkable.asserts: Mean of the i−a column over the 19 entries (about 3.63 arcseconds); descriptive only.
Change of the lower-microscope reading caused by 'Unteres Mikroskop geschoben' on April 28: 547.2'' − 206.6'' = 340.6'', i.e. about 5'40.6''.

transcription_corrections: In the April 26 row, column 2 shows '32,0' written with a correction (a digit overwritten); the reading is 3'32.0''.
In the May 6 row, column 1 '20,3' has an overwritten final digit.
In the May 9 row, column 2 '28,9' has an overwritten final digit.
In the May 13 row, column 2 '28,0' is overwritten (possibly corrected from 29).
The 'i−a' header is written above the fourth column, at the right, not as a separate line.
There is a faint marginal mark (possibly '64' or a tick) at the left beside the May 1 entries.
The April 24 entries carry explicit minute/second marks (9'20"9 4'11"5 3'22"8); several later fourth-column entries also carry the seconds mark (5"85, 3"55, 2"33).
